name: SikaTop Armatec-110 EpoCem

SIKATOP® ARMATEC®-110 EPOCEM®: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem®, May 2026, Version 05.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sikatop_armatec_-110epocem.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 05.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® is a three-part, cementitious, epoxy resin coating material. It contains a corrosion inhibitor and is used as a reinforcement corrosion protection and as a bonding primer. Based on EpoCem® technology, it offers superior bonding properties. SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® meets the requirement of EN 1504-7.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. As part of a concrete repair system, SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® is used as:
    - Bonding primer on concrete surfaces
    - Reinforcement corrosion protection
    - Control of anodic areas (Principle 11, method 11.1 of EN 1504-9), creating conditions in which potentially anodic cathodic areas of reinforcement are unable to take part
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Please note.
    - The Product is not suitable as a bonding primer for fast-setting concrete or fast-setting repair mortars

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem®
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Three-part epoxy-cement-based reinforcement corrosion protection and bonding primer
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - LEED v2009 IEQc 4.2 SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem®
    - LEED v4.1 MR: Material ingredients (option 2) and LEED v4.1 EQ: Low-emitting materials SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® en
    - Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) in accordance with EN 15804. EPD independently verified by Institut für Bauen und Umwelt e.V. (IBU)
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 1504-7:2006 Products and systems for the protection and repair of concrete structures — Reinforcement corrosion protection
    - Prüfungszeugnis Korrosionsschutzwirkung SikaTop Armatec-110 EpoCem, BAM
    - Test report Corrosion Protection EN 15183, iSK, No. UB300/07/08
    - Test report stress strain behaviour, EN 1766, Polymer Institut, No. P 2965
    - Carbon dioxide permeability of coating materials and systems EN 1062-6, SikaTop Armatec-110 EpoCem, LPM AG, Test Report No. A-40'046-1E
    - Chlorid Diffusion test report, Polymer Institut. No. P 3074
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-7: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Description (p.1); System Information > System structure (p.3).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - EN 15804: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Sustainability (p.1).
    - EN 1504-7:2006: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 15183: listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Technical Information > Corrosion test (p.2).
    - EN 1766: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1062-6: listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Technical Information > Diffusion resistance to carbon dioxide (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 15184: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear adhesion strength (p.2).
    - ISO 8501-1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > STEEL REINFORCEMENT (p.4).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Very good bonding properties
    - Compatible with most Sika MonoTop® and SikaEmaco® repair mortars
    - Very good adhesion to concrete and steel
    - Contains corrosion inhibitors
    - Very good resistance to water and chloride penetration
    - High shear strength
    - Long pot life
    - Easy to mix and apply
    - Can be applied by brush or spray gun
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Cement, epoxy resin, selected aggregates and additives
2.7 Colour.
    | Part A | White |
    | Part B | Colourless |
    | Part C | Dark grey |
    | Mixed components: dark grey |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Density.
    | Mixed density | 2.0 kg/L |
2.9 Appearance.
    | Part A | Liquid |
    | Part B | Liquid |
    | Part C | Powder |
2.10 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 18·10⁻⁶ 1/K (EN 1770)
    - Corrosion test: Pass (EN 15183)
2.11 Tensile adhesion strength.
    | after 28 days | ≥ 1.5 MPa |

    Test method printed: (EN 1542)
2.12 Shear adhesion strength.
    | Comparison of coated steel | Passed (≥ 80 %) |
    | to concrete to uncoated steel to concrete (pull-out test) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN 15184)

    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN 1062-6)
2.14 System structure. SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem® is a reinforcement corrosion protection primer in accordance with EN 1504-7 as part of the Sika® repair system. It is the first component of the system, followed by the application of Sika MonoTop® or SikaEmaco® concrete repair mortars.
2.15 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in undamaged original, sealed packaging; in dry cool conditions between +5 °C and +25 °C.
2.16 Packaging. 20 kg kit consisting of:
    | Part A | 1.14 kg container |
    | Part B | 2.86 kg container |
    | Part C | 16 kg bag |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 05.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Bonding primer. 1. Remove excess water from within the surface pores and cavities with a clean sponge. 2. Use a medium-hard brush or spray gun to apply the Product over the complete substrate surface. Press the Product well into the substrate to form a thin layer, filling surface pores or cavities. 3. Apply the subsequent layer of repair mortar wet on wet.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 05.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: The Product comes in pre-packed units with the correct mixing ratio.
4.3 Consumption. AS REINFORCEMENT CORROSION PROTECTION; For a total layer thickness of 2 mm, in two layers of 1 mm thickness each:
    | Rebar diameter | Amount of Product per metre |
    | 8 mm | 120 g/m (60 g/m per layer) |
    | 16 mm | 240 g/m (120 g/m per layer) |
    | AS BONDING PRIMER ON MINERAL SURFACES |
    | 1.5–2.0 kg powder per m² and mm layer thickness, depending on substrate conditions |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note: Consumption data is theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level, wastage or any other variations. Apply the Product to a test area to calculate the exact consumption for the specific substrate conditions and proposed application equipment.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | At +20 °C | 3 hours |
    | Pot life depends on temperature |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note: Pot life will be shorter at higher temperatures. Pot life will be longer at lower temperatures.
4.5 Application time. If applying the Product as bonding primer, respect the maximum waiting time before wet on wet application of Sika repair mortars and normal-setting concrete:
    | Temperature | Maximum waiting time |
    | +5 °C | 6 hours |
    | +10 °C | 4 hours |
    | +20 °C | 2 hours |
    | +30 °C | 1 hour |
4.6 Waiting time to overcoating. As reinforcement protection primer between first and second coat:
    | Temperature | Minimum waiting time |
    | +5 °C | 8–12 hours |
    | +10 °C | 4–6 hours |
    | +20 °C | 2–3 hours |
    | +30 °C | 1–2 hours |
    | As reinforcement protection primer between second coat and subsequent repair mortar application: |
    | Temperature | Minimum waiting time |
    | +5 °C | 30 hours |
    | +10 °C | 24 hours |
    | +20 °C | 18 hours |
    | +30 °C | 12 hours |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.7 Concrete. 1. Clean the substrate thoroughly so it is free from dust, loose material, surface contamination and material which reduces adhesion, prevents suction or wetting by the repair materials. 2. Remove delaminated, weak, damaged and deteriorated concrete and where necessary, sound concrete. Remove using mechanical hand-held tools, high or ultra-high-pressure water blasting equipment. 3. Remove sufficient concrete from around corroded reinforcement to allow cleaning, application of a corrosion protection coating (where required) and compaction of the concrete repair mortar. 4. Prepare repair surface areas in simple square or rectangular layouts to avoid shrinkage stress concentrations and cracking while the repair material cures. This can also avoid structural stress concentrations from thermal movement and loading during the service life.
4.8 Steel reinforcement. 1. Remove rust, scale, mortar, concrete, dust and other loose and deleterious material which reduces bond or contributes to corrosion. 2. Prepare surfaces to bright steel, Sa 2 (ISO 8501-1), using abrasive blast cleaning or high-pressure water blasting equipment.
4.9 Pre-wetting. Sufficient saturation of the concrete substrate prior to application enables the mortar to gain its full mechanical properties. 1. Thoroughly pre-wet the prepared concrete substrate for a minimum of 2 hours before application. 2. Keep the surface wet and do not allow to dry. 3. The final pre-wetted surface must achieve a dark matt appearance (saturated surface dry).
4.10 Mixing. 1. Shake parts A and B before opening. 2. Pour the liquid parts A and B into a clean mixing vessel. 3. Mix for 30 seconds with a low speed (< 250 rpm) electric drill mixer. 4. While mixing parts A and B, slowly add powder part C. Avoid entraining air. 5. IMPORTANT Do not add any water to the mix. Mix thoroughly for at least for 3 minutes until a uniform consistency is achieved. 6. Leave to stand for 5–10 minutes until the mixed coating material exhibits a brushable, weakly dripping consistency.
4.11 Important.
    - Strictly follow installation procedures
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in Method Statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
4.12 Important. Risk of cracking due to application in direct sun or strong winds 1. Do not apply the Product in direct sun, strong winds or both.
4.13 Reinforcement corrosion protection.
    - Preconditions
    - If using spray equipment, the substrate has been protected from overspray. 1. Use a clean brush or spraying equipment to apply a first coat 1 mm thick to cover the reinforcement bars. 2. When the first coat is fingernail-hard, apply a second coat 1 mm thick. 3. Wait until completely dry before applying repair mortar.
4.14 Curing treatment. Protect the fresh mortar from rain while the material has not yet set.
4.15 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically.
4.16 Further documentation.
    - Concrete repair site handbook
    - Sika Method Statement 850 32 01 Concrete Repair

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature.
    | Maximum | +30 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.3 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +30 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.4 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +30 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.5 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Note: Consumption data is theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level, wastage or any other variations. Apply the Product to a test area to calculate the exact consumption for the specific substrate conditions and proposed application equipment.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Tensile adhesion strength: after 28 days | ≥ 1.5 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 18·10⁻⁶ 1/K (EN 1770)
    - Corrosion test: Pass (EN 15183)
    - Shear adhesion strength: Comparison of coated steel | Passed (≥ 80 %); to concrete to uncoated steel to concrete (pull-out test) (EN 15184)
    - Diffusion resistance to carbon dioxide: for 1.9 mm of Product | Sd = 42 m (EN 1062-6)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaTop® Armatec®-110 EpoCem®, May 2026, Version 05.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sikatop_armatec_-110epocem.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTopÂ® ArmatecÂ®-110 EpoCemÂ® Part A, https://aus.sika.com/dam/dms/au01/3/sds-sikatop-armatec-110epocemparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
